newsitem.title: KENYA: ATHLETICS-KOMEN CONFIDENT OF BEATING GEBRSELASSIE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMEN CONFIDENT OF BEATING GEBRSELASSIE.

text.p: Kenyan distance ace Daniel Komen feels certain he will beat Ethiopian world record holder Haile Gebrselassie if they meet in the 5,000 metres at the World Championships in Athens next month.
He sees it as part of Kenya's necessary atonement for their poor showing at last year's Olympics in Atlanta, when they won just one gold medal.
"I think we must make a point," Komen said after winning the 5,000 metres at the Kenyan trials on Saturday.
"In Athens, Kenyans must win. Of course there will be competition. There are the Moroccans, there are the Ethiopians. Personally, I am confident I shall win.".
Komen suggested after Saturday's victory that Gebreselassie had been avoiding him in European Grand Prix meetings in the last few months.

"I will meet with Gebrselassie, then we shall see who is who. I am confident I shall win," Komen said after clocking 13 minutes 23.8 seconds, beating Tom Nyariki's 13:25.1 and Paul Bitok, timed in 13:27.0.
Komen and world steeplechase champion and record-holder Moses Kiptanui are seen as the men to restore Kenya's reputation as Africa's top athletics nation.
Kiptanui said he ill last year but stronger now.
"This year, I am okay. But I have been unbeatable at this distance since 1991.
"I will win a fourth (World Championship) in Athens. Then I will hang on until the Sydney Olympics. As you well know, I have no Olympics medal," he added.

Commonwealth 800 metres champion Patrick Konchellah, whose career was nearly ended by a car accident in 1995, said meanwhile he felt he was the only person who could stop Kenyan-born Dane Wilson Kipketer.
Konchellah, brother of track veteran Billy Konchellah, said he had beaten Kipketer before and would again.
"I started training a month ago. So I am going to be in great shape in a few weeks. Kipketer? I am not worried. I am about the only one who can stop him," Konchellah added.
Officials have delayed naming the team until July 16.
Kenya's only gold in Atlanta went to Josephat Keter in the steeplechase.
But he was well beaten in the trials, where other notables to fail included middle and long distance stars Ishmael Kirui, William Tanui, Fred Oyancha, Patrick Sang and Martin Keino.
Paul Koech, Dominic Kirui and Paul Tergat are vying for slots available for the 10,000 metres, while Laban Rotich, John Kobowen and Stephen Kipkario look to the 1,500 metres.
Kennedy Ochieng has taken over as Kenya's leading one-lap runner while Erick Keter looks to a 400 metres hurdles medal.
"Without Michael Johnson in Athens, no one can genuinely claim that the gold belongs to them. It is open. I could get it," Ochieng said.

Among Kenya's women, Olympic silver medallist Pauline Konga is missing from the 5,000 metres lineup that has Lydia Cheromei and Jepkemboi Barsosio. Jepkemboi's sister Sally Barsosio leads the 10,000 metres that also includes Margaret Okaya.
